quotes.quote: we introduce LifeSearch, a challenging benchmark comprising 203 Chinese and English tasks derived from real-user query seeds across 7 concrete life and productivity domains
existing benchmarks provide limited coverage of real-world life and professional productivity settings
L IFE S EARCH comprises 203 tasks (102 in Chinese and 101 in English) across seven real-world personal and professional productivity domains.
We use an LLM to classify the retained queries by their core purpose into seven productivity domains
Candidate queries may combine information seeking with operational actions such as generating local files or interactive HTML visualizations.
Finally, experts consolidate the refined subtasks into a coherent query grounded in a concrete life or work scenario.
The benchmark contains 4,014 rubrics, averaging 19.8 per task.
Approximately 40% of the rubrics explicitly specify numerical values, specific events, or named documents, which provide concrete targets for verification.

The denominator sums the weights of all rubrics in the task (including unmet ones), requiring a positive total weight for well-defined normalization; zero-weight rubrics are omitted.
we select Gemini 3.1 Pro with low reasoning effort and zero temperature, which achieves the highest mean accuracy (84.25%) among the tested configurations on these 402 labels
reaching a substantial inter-annotator agreement (mean pairwise Cohen’s κ = 0.715)
We evaluate frontier Deep Research agents on L IFE S EARCH to assess their ability to complete real-world tasks and examine agreement between aggregate scores and human report rankings.

We evaluate 12 frontier DR agents on all 203 bilingual tasks: GPT-5.6 Sol, Claude Opus 5, Hy4 Preview, GLM-5.3, Qwen3.8-Max, DeepSeek-V4 Pro, Kimi-K3, Doubao-Seed-2.1-Pro, Claude Opus 4.8, Hy3, GLM-5.2, and Gemini-3.6-Flash.
All systems operate within a shared ReAct-style (Yao et al., 2023) harness that interleaves decisions, tool execution, and feedback from the resulting observations.
We use Serper1 as the web-search backend and Jina Reader2 to retrieve web pages.
GPT-5.6 Sol leads with 63.4%, followed by Claude Opus 5 at 56.1%; all other systems score below 50%.
These differences are descriptive, especially for the nine-task everyday-facts subset.
Hy4 Preview reaches a comparable score to GLM-5.3 (49.7% versus 49.2%) with only 33.6k tokens.
Premature clarification. Doubao-Seed-2.1-Pro and GPT-5.6 Sol sometimes ask follow-up questions instead of proceeding with the research task.
Temporal scope violations. Agents sometimes default to current web data even when the query specifies an earlier cutoff, a behavior particularly noticeable in Hy4 Preview.
Missing required details. With around 20 rubrics per task, a fluent summary can address the broad topic while omitting requested entities, numerical values, dates, sources, or edge cases.
human rankings are strongly correlated (Spearman’s ρ = 0.89, Kendall’s τ = 0.81), with identical ordering of the top four systems
Comparison of L IFE S EARCH with representative Deep Research benchmarks.
Comparison of 11 judge configurations on 402 human-labeled rubrics for judge selection,
Scores are reported as mean ± sample standard deviation across three independent agent runs.
Financial market analysis: stock, futures, fund, foreign-exchange, or index valuation; trends; stock picking; arbitrage; and market moves.
All models listed in the table are evaluated within a few days of one another in August 2026.
Task and rubric wording is reproduced from the dataset, and rubric numbers follow their original order.
We hired crowd workers to write the initial query seeds for L IFE S EARCH. All candidate queries undergo privacy screening and anonymization before task construction.
We use ChatGPT solely for language refinement of the manuscript's text.
Yibo Wang, Senjie Jin, Yansong Ning, Xinbing Liang, Haotian Luo, Jiazheng Zhang, Yuxuan HE, Will WU, Clarenceai
